land.text: the Eyalet of Tunis, which the Husainid bey took over from the Ottoman province

predecessors.note: The infobox lists 'Preceded by: Eyalet of Tunis'; the Husainid page says the dynasty 'originally ruled under the suzerainty of the Ottoman Empire' and was regarded by the sultans as beylerbeyi. Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire row is a neighbour 1706-1712 and 1836-1839.

land.text: Tunisia, a French protectorate from 12 May 1881

successors.note: The Bey remained 'nominally independent' head of state to 1956; the Husainid monarchy was abolished on 25 July 1957. Cliopatria's French Africa covers Tunisia only from 1885, so 1882-1884 is uncovered unless the French dossier draws the protectorate from 1881.

capitals.name: Tunis
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Tunis'; the Bardo palace was the seat of the treaty.

rulers.name: Ali I (Abu'l Hasan)
rulers.note: 7 September 1735 - 22 September 1756; overthrown by two sons of his predecessor.

rulers.name: Muhammad III as-Sadiq
rulers.note: 22 September 1859 - 27 October 1882 (Husainid page), so he was bey at the Treaty of Bardo in May 1881. Capped at the dossier's end (12 May 1881); he reigned on under the protectorate to 1882 (reviewer af-02-e).

keyframe_review.note: 79,457 km2, northern and central Tunisia. Husayn bin Ali 'seized power in a coup' in July 1705 (10 July in the body, 15 July in the infobox), a year before Cliopatria's row; the shape is unchanged but should hold from July 1705. The page gives no area; the French protectorate page's 155,000 km2 for 1881 is the nearest figure (see the 1880 shape).

correction.text: the beylik's land unchanged, holding from July 1705

keyframe_review.note: 79,482 km2 (+25 km2, noise). The Hammuda Pasha Bey page opened is the 17th-century Muradid ruler, not Hammuda ibn Ali (1782-1814): it says Djerba once belonged to the pasha of Tripoli and that Tunis 'definitively annexed' it during his reign, so Djerba is Tunisian before 1705. No page explains the 1709 change.

79,383 km2, -99 km2 for 1757-1761, back to 79,482 in 1762. In September 1756 Ali I was overthrown by two sons of his predecessor, who 'took Tunis with help from the governor of Constantine'; the page gives no territory change, so the dip is unexplained (a border strip with Algiers is the likely cause).
79,482 km2: the 1709 shape again; no territorial event on the page between 1756 and 1794.

87,930 km2, +8,448 km2 (bbox south edge 33.14 -> 32.49 N, east edge 11.08 -> 11.54 E): a strip near Ben Gardane and Dehiba on the Tripolitanian side, which Cliopatria draws as Karamanli land until 1793 (Karamanli shape 1762-1793: 85,534 km2; 76,381 km2 from 1794) and as Tunisian from 1794. Unverified: no page opened dates or explains the transfer. The Tripolitanian civil war page has Ali Burghul seize Tripoli on 29-30 July 1793 and occupy Djerba on 30 September 1794, and Yusuf and Hamet Karamanli retake Tripoli on 19 January 1795 'with the aid of the Bey of Tunis'.
87,831 km2 (-99 km2, noise): Tripoli restored under the Karamanlis in 1795-1797 with Tunisian help; the border strip stays Tunisian in the shape.
87,806 km2 (-25 km2). 'French forces occupied central coastal Algeria in 1830' (page); Constantine is not mentioned. No territorial change for Tunis is dated.
87,956 km2 (+150 km2). Ahmad Bey's reforms (conscription, the Bardo Military Academy of 1840, the slave-trade ban of 1841, abolition on 23 January 1846) are internal; no border change on the page.
87,980 km2 (+24 km2): noise; no territorial event on the page.

88,079 km2 (+99 km2): noise. Muhammad III as-Sadiq succeeded on 22 September 1859 (Husainid page); the 1864 Mejba revolt and the 1869 bankruptcy and Anglo-Franco-Italian financial commission are not territorial.
87,905 km2 (-174 km2): noise; the 1869 bankruptcy created an international financial commission but no border change.

87,905 km2 for 1880-1884, against the French protectorate page's 'area of 155,000 square kilometres' (ratio 0.57, within the factor of two; the shape omits the Saharan south, whose 'southern border with the Sahara' the page calls ill-defined). The Treaty of Bardo of 12 May 1881 gave France foreign affairs and finances and the right to station troops; the Bey stayed head of state, 'deemed nominally independent'. The shape should hold to 12 May 1881; 1881-1884 is the protectorate (drawn by French Africa, which in Cliopatria covers Tunisia only from 1885).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, holding until 12 May 1881; after that the French protectorate

ledger.note: July 1705: Husayn bin Ali seizes power at Tunis and founds the Husainid beylik. 'Husayn bin Ali seized power in a coup' (10 July 1705 in the body, 15 July in the infobox; the Husainid page: 'Founded 15 July 1705'); preceded by the Eyalet of Tunis.

region.text: a strip near Ben Gardane and Dehiba that Cliopatria moves from the Karamanli shape to Tunis in 1794

ledger.note: 1794: a strip on the Tripolitanian frontier passes to Tunis (page silent). Bridging judgment from Cliopatria's shapes only (Karamanli loses the strip in 1794, Tunis gains it). The page gives only: Burghul occupied Djerba on 30 September 1794; Hammuda 'received the Karamanlis well' and the Karamanlis regained Tripoli on 19 January 1795 'with the aid of the Bey of Tunis'.

region.text: the north-west and Bizerte, where the French entered

ledger.note: 24 April 1881: French troops enter Tunisia from the north. They 'entered Tunisia from the north on 24 April 1881 and landed at Bizerte from 1 May' on the pretext of the Khroumir raid of 30-31 March.

region.text: Tunisia, under the Treaty of Bardo

ledger.note: 12 May 1881: the Treaty of Bardo. France takes foreign affairs and finances and may station troops; the Bey 'could not conclude international acts without French permission'. Risings at Sfax (27 June, retaken 16 July), Gabes (30 July) and Kairouan (August to 26 October) follow; Tunis is occupied on 10 October.

region.text: the beylik, now a French protectorate

ledger.note: 12 May 1881: the Treaty of Bardo ends the independent beylik. Tunisia becomes a French protectorate, 'deemed nominally independent' under the Bey (the Convention of La Marsa, 1883, is on the page without a day); the Husainid line lasts to 25 July 1957, when Bourguiba declares a republic. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1884.

wars.name: Algerian intervention in Tunis (1756)
wars.outcome: Ali I was overthrown by two sons of his predecessor, who 'took Tunis with help from the governor of Constantine'; Muhammad I ar-Rashid reigned from 22 September 1756.
wars.note: No territory is named on the page.

wars.name: Tripolitanian civil war

zones.text: Djerba, occupied by Ali Burghul on 30 September 1794

wars.outcome: Burghul seized Tripoli on 29-30 July 1793 and 'occupied Djerba, an island under Tunisian jurisdiction, on 30 September 1794'; on 19 January 1795 the Karamanlis retook Tripoli with the aid of the Bey of Tunis. The page reports no Tunisian occupation of Tripolitanian land.
wars.note: Djerba is not in the gazetteer; a radius is used. The end of Burghul's occupation of the island is not dated on the page, so no occupation pair is written.

wars.name: Hammouda's war with Algiers (1807)
wars.outcome: 'Hammouda I's forces ended Algerian attempts to overthrow the beys' in 1807; no territory changed hands on the page.
wars.note: The page is silent on the 1813-14 Algerian invasions.

wars.name: French invasion of Tunisia (1881)
wars.outcome: The French entered from the north on 24 April and landed at Bizerte from 1 May 1881; the Treaty of Bardo (12 May) made Tunisia a protectorate; the Sfax rising (27 June) was put down on 16 July, Gabes retaken on 30 July, Kairouan on 26 October, and Tunis occupied on 10 October.
wars.note: The pretext was the Khroumir raid of 30-31 March 1881.

certainty.note: The pages give no treaty frontier: the Algerian frontier is mentioned but not described, the Tripolitanian frontier is not on the pages, and the Saharan south is 'ill-defined'; the northern and coastal limits are firmer than the desert.

notes: Beylik of Tunis (af-02-e). (1) End year: the dossier ends on 12 May 1881 (Bardo: France takes foreign affairs and finances), but the Husainid line stayed 'nominally independent' head of state until 1956-57 and Cliopatria keeps the row to 1884; Cliopatria's French Africa covers Tunisia only from 1885 (137k km2) and just 4 cells before, so 1882-1884 is uncovered unless the French Africa dossier (af-08) draws Tunisia as a protectorate (rule 4 vassal tint) from 1881. (2) Ottoman suzerainty: the Husainids 'originally ruled under the suzerainty of the Ottoman Empire' (Husainid page), 'formally part of the Ottoman Empire' (Beylik page); neither gives an end date. The vassal_start and vassal_end belong in the Ottoman dossier (me-10) with counterpart beylik-of-tunis; none is written here. (3) The 1794 shape (+8.4k km2 on the Tripolitanian side, taken from the Karamanli shape) is not explained by any page opened; the ledger records it at confidence 1. (4) The Hammuda Pasha Bey page opened was the 17th-century Muradid ruler, not Hammuda ibn Ali (1782-1814), whom the research wanted: it is listed in sources with that caveat and its Djerba statement is used only for pre-1705 Djerba; the 18th-century bey's article was not opened (page budget). (5) The Beylik page's infobox bey list is inconsistent with its body (Rejeb Khaznadar and Mustapha Ben Ismail are prime ministers, not beys); the Husainid page's list is used. Pages silent: Genoese Tabarka (1741), the 1735 and 1813-14 Algerian invasions, Constantine, the Convention of La Marsa day, the Ottoman suzerainty's end, the Tunisian-Tripolitanian frontier, any area figure for the beylik (the protectorate page gives 155,000 km2 for the French period). (6) Gazetteer names lacking: Djerba (radius used).
